name: opcua-mcp-server
description: Read industrial sensors and control equipment on any OPC UA server.
long_description:
Connects Claude to any OPC UA server — a PLC, a SCADA gateway, a historian or a simulator — and exposes it as MCP tools.

Set the endpoint below to your OPC UA server's URL. The default **observe** profile can read, browse and monitor but cannot write, call methods or acknowledge alarms. Use **operator** with explicit target allowlists for production control; **full** is intended for a tightly scoped OPC UA account.

**Security:** the connection defaults to unencrypted and anonymous for local simulation. Control tools remain blocked on an insecure channel unless the lab-only override is enabled. Against real equipment, set Basic256Sha256, a client certificate and key, and credentials scoped to exactly the nodes and methods required.

opcua_server_url.title: OPC UA endpoint
opcua_server_url.description: URL of the OPC UA server to connect to, including any path the server expects. Read once at startup: one process serves one endpoint. Nothing verifies who answers at this address unless the server certificate is pinned.

opcua_security_policy.title: Security policy
opcua_security_policy.description: Encryption suite to negotiate for the secure channel. Anything other than None needs a client certificate and key. The two AES suites are Node-only: the Python runtime refuses them at startup rather than downgrading. One of: None, Basic128Rsa15, Basic256, Basic256Sha256, Aes128_Sha256_RsaOaep, Aes256_Sha256_RsaPss. None is unencrypted and unauthenticated, and keeps control tools blocked unless insecure control is explicitly allowed. An unknown policy stops the server at startup. Leave blank for None.

opcua_security_mode.title: Security mode
opcua_security_mode.description: Message security mode for the secure channel. Sign authenticates messages without encrypting them. One of: None, Sign, SignAndEncrypt. A policy with mode None, or a mode without a policy, stops the server at startup; leaving it blank never downgrades a policy to signing only. Leave blank for SignAndEncrypt once a security policy is set, otherwise None.

opcua_client_cert.title: Client certificate
opcua_client_cert.description: Path to the certificate (PEM or DER) this client presents as its application identity. Required by any security policy other than None. A path that does not exist stops the server at startup.

opcua_client_key.title: Client private key
opcua_client_key.description: Path to the private key matching the client certificate. A path, never key material. Whoever can read the file can impersonate this client: keep it readable only by the account running the server. A path that does not exist stops the server at startup.

opcua_application_uri.title: Application URI
opcua_application_uri.description: Application URI announced to the server. Set it only for a certificate that carries no URI of its own: a server may reject a session whose URI does not match the certificate. Leave blank for the subjectAltName URI of the client certificate.

opcua_server_cert.title: Pinned server certificate
opcua_server_cert.description: Path to the OPC UA server's own certificate (PEM or DER), pinned: a server presenting any other certificate cannot complete the handshake. Requires a security policy other than None. Unset, encryption protects against eavesdropping but not against an impostor endpoint. Set without a security policy, it stops the server at startup rather than pinning nothing.

opcua_username.title: Username
opcua_username.description: OPC UA username. The session is anonymous when unset. Cannot be combined with a user certificate. Requires a password; either one alone stops the server at startup.

opcua_password.title: Password
opcua_password.description: Password for the username. Without a security policy it crosses the network in clear text. Supply it through the client's secret storage, never on a command line.

opcua_user_cert.title: User certificate
opcua_user_cert.description: Path to the certificate identifying the user, for X.509 user authentication: a different key pair from the client certificate, which secures the channel. Requires the user key and a security policy other than None; cannot be combined with a username. Any of those combinations broken stops the server at startup.

opcua_user_key.title: User private key
opcua_user_key.description: Path to the private key for the user certificate. It signs the server's challenge and is never sent. Whoever can read the file can log in as this user: keep it readable only by the account running the server.

opcua_profile.title: Tool profile
opcua_profile.description: Which tools are offered. observe reads, browses, reads history and monitors; operator adds explicitly allowlisted writes, method calls and alarm actions; full exposes every tool and is meant only for a tightly scoped OPC UA account. One of: observe, operator, full (read-only and readonly mean observe). Unset fails closed to observe; an unknown profile stops the server at startup.

opcua_policy_file.title: Policy file
opcua_policy_file.description: Path to a version-1 JSON policy file, the only place per-node value bounds can be set. Every policy variable that is set overrides what the file says. An unreadable or invalid file stops the server at startup.

opcua_allowed_tools.title: Allowed tools
opcua_allowed_tools.description: Comma-separated tool allowlist. It can only narrow the selected profile, never widen it. An unknown tool name stops the server at startup.

opcua_allowed_write_nodes.title: Writable node IDs
opcua_allowed_write_nodes.description: Comma-separated exact node IDs the operator profile may write, as ns=2;i=5 or, stable across a server restart, nsu=<namespace-uri>;i=5. Setting it replaces the policy file's list, bounds included. Empty fails closed: operator can write nothing. A batch write with any target outside the list is refused before it reaches OPC UA.

opcua_allowed_methods.title: Callable methods
opcua_allowed_methods.description: Comma-separated object_node_id|method_node_id pairs the operator profile may call. Empty fails closed: operator can call nothing. An entry without | stops the server at startup.

opcua_allow_acknowledge_alarms.title: Allow alarm actions
opcua_allow_acknowledge_alarms.description: Let the operator profile act on alarms: acknowledge_alarm and every act_on_alarm action.

opcua_allow_insecure_control.title: Allow insecure control (lab only)
opcua_allow_insecure_control.description: Permit control tools on an OPC UA channel with no security policy. Fail-open override: writes, method calls and alarm actions then travel unauthenticated and unencrypted. Never enable it against production equipment.

opcua_allow_out_of_range_writes.title: Allow writes outside EURange
opcua_allow_out_of_range_writes.description: Allow a write outside the EURange the OPC UA server itself published for the node. Fail-open override: it discards the only value bound a deployment with no policy file has.

opcua_audit_file.title: Audit file
opcua_audit_file.description: Path to an append-only file for the control audit trail, one JSON object per line, written beside stderr. Created if it does not exist. A file that cannot be opened stops the server rather than falling back to stderr alone.

opcua_operator_id.title: Operator label
opcua_operator_id.description: Label stamped on every audit record, so a shipped log says which deployment a control call came from. A label, not a verified identity.

opcua_reconnect_initial_delay_ms.title: First retry delay (ms)
opcua_reconnect_initial_delay_ms.description: Wait before the first attempt to repair a dropped or refused connection, in milliseconds. It doubles with each further attempt. Leave blank for 1000.

opcua_reconnect_max_delay_ms.title: Longest retry delay (ms)
opcua_reconnect_max_delay_ms.description: Ceiling for the doubling retry delay, in milliseconds. Leave blank for 8000.

opcua_reconnect_max_retry.title: Reconnection attempts
opcua_reconnect_max_retry.description: Retries after the first attempt before a tool call gives up. 0 never retries; -1 retries forever. Leave blank for 3.

opcua_session_timeout_ms.title: Session timeout (ms)
opcua_session_timeout_ms.description: Session lifetime asked of the OPC UA server, in milliseconds. It also sets the keep-alive period, so it decides how quickly an idle connection notices the server has gone. Leave blank for 60000.

io.github.industriagents/opcua-mcp.generated: user_config and server.mcp_config.env are generated from contract/config.json by packages/server-node/scripts/config-artifacts.mjs. Edit the schema and run `npm run config:generate` in packages/server-node; CI fails if they drift.
